s1.syndrome_frame: febrile skin lesions with neutropenia and recent chemotherapy
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
purpura and erythematous and edematous ring on the right chest
key_facts: tender lesions on the neck and trunk
recent first cycle of chemotherapy (ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone)
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry: Positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

raw.syndrome_frame: febrile skin lesions with neutropenia and recent chemotherapy
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
purpura and erythematous and edematous ring on the right chest
key_facts: tender lesions on the neck and trunk
recent first cycle of chemotherapy (ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone)
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry: Positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of multiple myeloma and recent chemotherapy, and skin biopsy showed myeloperoxidase-positive cells, suggesting leukemia cutis

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with febrile skin lesions, neutropenia, and recent chemotherapy, which are consistent with Sweet syndrome

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neutropenia and recent chemotherapy, which are risk factors for neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis

shortlist.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neutropenia and recent chemotherapy, which are risk factors for ecthyma gangrenosum

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with febrile skin lesions and recent chemotherapy, which are consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions, and laboratory findings of leukopenia and elevated C-reactive protein, along with the skin biopsy showing an inflammatory infiltrate and positive immunohistochemistry for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, are consistent with Sweet syndrome, particularly in the context of recent chemotherapy and neutropenia.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: The immunohistochemistry was negative for CD138, which is more commonly associated with plasma cell dyscrasias like multiple myeloma, and the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells does not necessarily indicate leukemia cutis in this context.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by neutrophilic infiltration around eccrine glands, which was not specifically noted in the skin biopsy findings.

rejected.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
rejected.why: This condition is typically associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, and the blood culture was negative, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar skin lesions, the biopsy findings and laboratory results do not specifically support this diagnosis over Sweet syndrome.
